title: Why even + even is even
summary: A compact proof that shows how structure helps us reason about numbers.

steps.justification: Any even number can be written as two times another integer.
steps.visualHint: Think of two pairs of tiles: each pair is a whole group of 2.

steps.justification: Factor out the common factor of 2.
steps.visualHint: When you combine the groups, you still have groups of 2.

steps.statement: Since $a + b$ is an integer, $2(a + b)$ is even.
steps.justification: A number of the form $2k$ is even by definition.
steps.visualHint: The result is still made of complete pairs.

title: Why addition is commutative
summary: A short proof that rearranging addends does not change the total.

steps.justification: Addition combines two quantities into one total.
steps.visualHint: Imagine a row of $a$ blocks and a row of $b$ blocks.

steps.statement: Reorder the blocks to form $b + a$.
steps.justification: The same blocks are still present, just arranged in a different order.
steps.visualHint: Slide the two rows so the order changes but the number of blocks stays the same.

steps.statement: The total number of blocks is unchanged.
steps.justification: Counting the same objects in a different order does not change the quantity.
steps.visualHint: Count the blocks carefully: the total is still the same.

title: Why $a(b + c) = ab + ac$
summary: A visual proof that shows how multiplication distributes across addition.

steps.justification: The expression $a(b + c)$ means a copies of the combined quantity $b + c$.
steps.visualHint: Picture $a$ identical rows of two blocks each.

steps.statement: Split each row into $b$ and $c$ parts.
steps.justification: Each row contains $b$ pieces and $c$ pieces.
steps.visualHint: Separate the row into a left section and a right section.

steps.justification: You have $a$ copies of $b$ plus $a$ copies of $c$.
steps.visualHint: Count the left section and the right section separately.
